newsitem.title: SWITZERLAND: Swiss welcome Nazi gold report, says lacks context.
newsitem.headline: Swiss welcome Nazi gold report, says lacks context.

text.p: Switzerland welcomed a U.S. report on Wednesday criticising Swiss gold transactions with Nazi Germany as a contribution to clearing up the country's World War Two history.

But Foreign Minister Flavio Cotti said in a statement the mammoth report appeared to lack historical context about the difficult circumstances Switzerland faced as a small neutral country surrounded by Axis powers during the war.

"The Federal Council (cabinet) welcomes the efforts of those responsible for the report to present facts objectively," Cotti said. "But on first reading it finds lacking an appropriate appreciation of the extremely difficult situation in which our country found itself at that time militarily and in terms of supplies."

He said the report confirmed figures about gold transactions that the Swiss central bank and historians had already aired, but noted it also suggested Germany sold Switzerland gold robbed from invididual Holocaust victims, not just official stocks.

"If this is really true, this a deeply shocking turn of events. It is nearly incomprehensible for us to see the cynicism and cold-bloodedness with which Nazi thugs re-smelted their victims' gold and re-sold it as regular central bank gold," he said, noting Swiss central bankers had been unaware of this.

Cotti said the report gave Switzerland credit for taking steps to probe its wartime history and called on countries to work together to investigate the past. "We want the truth and justice. Investigations must be conducted openly and without conditions in all countries affected. Switzerland is ready for this and has already introduced the necessary steps."
